faq.title: Frequently asked questions about QR codes
faq.subtitle: Clear answers about how to create, use and print QR codes for free.

items.q: What types of QR codes can I create?
items.a: You can create codes for [links (URL)](/generador-qr/url), [WhatsApp](/generador-qr/whatsapp), [WiFi networks](/generador-qr/wifi), [text](/generador-qr/texto), [Google reviews](/generador-qr/resenas-google), [contact cards](/generador-qr/vcard), [locations](/generador-qr/ubicacion) and [email](/generador-qr/email). For all of them you can choose the color and size, and add a logo. For now there are no other types, such as calendar events.

items.q: Does it cost anything, or is there a limit on codes?
items.a: It costs nothing and there is no limit on codes. There is no paid version either. If it helped you, you can support the project with a [voluntary donation](/donaciones).

items.q: Do I need an account or to give my email?
items.a: No. There is no sign-up or accounts. You come in, create the code and download it. We do not ask for your email either.

items.q: Do QR codes expire?
items.a: No. They are static: the content is stored inside the code, not on a server, so they do not expire or have a scan limit. They only stop being useful if the content stops existing, for example a website that is deleted or a WiFi password that you change.

items.q: Can I edit a code I already printed?
items.a: No. In a static code the content is fixed in the pattern. To change it you have to create a new code. Dynamic codes can be edited, but they depend on an intermediate service, an account and, normally, a payment. We explain it in more detail on the [home page](/).

items.q: Do I need internet to create or scan a code?
items.a: You need internet to load this page. After that, the code is created on your device, without sending what you type to any server. You do not need internet to scan it: the phone reads the code on its own. Of course, if the code leads to a website, the phone will need internet to open it.

items.q: Do you store the content of my codes?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device, so what you type is not sent to any server and we never see it. Google Analytics counts page visits, but it does not receive the content of your codes.

items.q: Where is my history stored?
items.a: Only in your browser, on this device. We do not see it. You can check it in the [History](/history) section and delete it whenever you want. If you clear your browser data, it disappears.

items.q: What data does the site collect?
items.a: We use Google Analytics to count visits in general, and we store your language and theme (light or dark) on your device. We do not show ads. You can see the details in the [privacy policy](/privacy).

items.q: Which format should I download the code in?
items.a: There are four: PNG, JPG, SVG and PDF. Use SVG for print shops and large sizes, because it scales without losing quality. Use PNG or JPG for screens and social media. The PDF is useful to print the code on an A4 sheet.

items.q: What file size can I choose?
items.a: From 200 to 2000 pixels. For screens, 300 to 500 is enough. For printing, choose 1000 or more, or use the SVG format.

items.q: What size and colors should I use so it scans well?
items.a: Print the code at least 2 x 2 cm, and bigger if it will be scanned from far away. The background is always white, so choose a dark color for the dots. Light or low-contrast colors make scanning fail. Test with your phone before printing many copies.

items.q: Can I put my logo in the center?
items.a: Yes. Turn on the logo option and upload a PNG, JPG or GIF image of up to 10 MB. The codes use the highest level of error correction, which allows a small part to be covered. Use a simple logo and check that the code reads well.

staticVsDynamic.title: Static vs. dynamic QR: which one fits you
staticVsDynamic.intro: There are two kinds of QR codes. They look alike, but they work differently.

static.title: Static QR
static.badge: This is the one this tool creates
points: The content is written inside the code.
The code is created on your device: what you type is not sent to any server.
The phone reads the content directly, without going through any server of ours.
It never expires and has no scan limit.
You do not need an account or a subscription.
It cannot be changed once printed. If the content changes, you create a new code.

dynamic.title: Dynamic QR
points: The code holds a short address. When scanned, it goes through an intermediate server that sends you to the destination.
You can change the destination without changing the printed code.
It normally requires an account and, often, a paid subscription.
If you cancel or the trial ends, the code may stop working.

choose.title: When to choose each one
choose.static: Choose a static QR if the content will not change: a WiFi network, a WhatsApp chat, a text or a website that will stay at the same address. It is the simplest option and depends on nobody.
choose.dynamic: Choose a dynamic QR if you will print many copies of something that will change, such as a menu you update every week, or if you need to count how many people scan it. For that you will need a service with an account, which is usually paid.

whatIs.title: What is a QR code?
paragraphs: A QR code is a square of dots that stores information: a link, a phone number, a text or the details of a WiFi network. To read it, you just point your phone camera at it. On most current phones you do not need to install any app.
QR stands for “Quick Response”. It was created in 1994 by a Japanese company to track parts in a car factory. Today it is used on menus, posters, business cards and packages.

The codes from this tool use the highest level of error correction. That is why they can be read even if they get a little dirty, if part of them is damaged or if they have a logo in the center. Still, always check that it scans well before printing.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: These are the most common doubts before creating a code.

items.q: Is it really free?
items.a: Yes. Creating and downloading QR codes is free and there is no limit on the number of codes. There is no paid version and no watermark. The project is kept alive with voluntary donations, which are never required.

items.q: Do QR codes expire?
items.a: No. They are static codes: the content is inside the code, so it does not expire or have a scan limit. A link code will only stop reaching its destination if that website disappears or changes address.

items.q: Do I need to sign up or give my email?
items.a: No. There are no accounts or sign-up, and we do not ask for your email either. You type the details, generate the code and download it.

items.q: Which formats can I download the code in?
items.a: PNG, JPG, SVG and PDF. To print large or send it to a print shop, SVG is best because it does not lose quality when enlarged. For screens and social media, PNG or JPG work well.

items.q: Can I change the content after printing the code?
items.a: No. The content stays inside the code and cannot be edited. If you need to change it, create a new code and replace the printed one. If you know it will change often, a dynamic QR may suit you, although it usually requires an account and payment.

items.q: Do you store what I type into my codes?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device: what you type is not sent to any server. Google Analytics counts page visits, but it does not receive the content of your codes. The history is saved only in your browser and you can delete it whenever you want.

items.q: Can I use the codes in my business?
items.a: Yes. The terms of use allow personal and commercial use, and the codes you create are yours. You are responsible for the content you put inside them.

items.q: What size should I use for printing?
items.a: At least about 2 x 2 cm, and bigger if it will be scanned from far away. Download a large file (for example, 1000 pixels) or an SVG so it does not look blurry when enlarged. Always test with your phone before printing many copies.

url.other: Turn a website, a menu or a profile into a code.
url.lead: Turn any link into a free QR code. It works for a website, a PDF menu, your social media profile or a reviews page. No sign-up, no ads and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a QR code for a link

steps.title: Copy the full link
steps.text: Open the page in your browser and copy the address from the top bar. It should start with https:// so the phone recognizes it as a link.

steps.title: Paste it and customize the code
steps.text: Paste the address in the URL field. If you want, change the color and size or add your logo. Pick a dark color: the background is always white, so it scans better.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone to see that it opens the right page. Then download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

about.title: What a link QR does
paragraphs: A link QR stores a web address inside the code. When someone scans it with the camera, the phone offers to open that address in the browser. Nothing has to be typed, even if the address is long.

This code is static: the address is written in the pattern and does not go through any server of ours when scanned. That is why it does not expire or count scans. In exchange, you cannot change the destination after printing it, so check the link carefully before downloading.

useCases.title: What a link QR is for
useCases.intro: These are some common uses. In all of them, the link must be a public address that will not change.

items.title: Restaurant menu
items.text: Publish the PDF menu on a website or on a file service with a public link, and put the code on the tables. Customers open it without downloading anything.

items.title: Google reviews
items.text: If you have a Google business profile, you can copy the link to ask for reviews and turn it into a code. Put it on the counter or on the receipt.

items.title: Social media
items.text: Put a code on your card, in your shop window or on your packaging that leads to your Instagram, TikTok or Facebook profile.

items.title: Catalog or online shop
items.text: Link your PDF catalog or your shop page on flyers and posters, so it can be opened from the street.

items.title: Use short links
items.text: The longer the link, the more dots the code has and the harder it is to read. If yours is very long, use a shorter address on your own website.

items.title: Start with https://
items.text: Always include the https:// or http:// at the start. Without it, some phones treat the content as text and not as a link.

items.title: Test the page on your phone
items.text: Scan the code with your phone, not only from the computer. Check that the page looks good on a small screen.

items.title: Pick a stable address
items.text: If you later move the page to another address, the printed code will stop leading to it. Think of an address that will last before you print.

items.q: Does a link QR code expire?
items.a: No. The code has the address written inside and does not depend on our website. It will work as long as the page it points to still exists.

items.q: Can I change the link after printing the code?
items.a: No. This generator creates static codes and the link cannot be edited. If you need another destination, create a new code. If you will change it often, you need a dynamic QR, which usually requires an account and a subscription.

items.q: Can I make a QR for a PDF or an image?
items.a: Yes, but first you have to upload the file to the internet and copy its public link, for example from your own website or from a storage service that lets you share with a link. Then paste that link here. This generator does not host files.

items.q: How many times can it be scanned?
items.a: As many as you want. Since the code does not go through our server, we do not count scans. If you need statistics, measure them on the destination page with your own analytics tool.

items.q: Can I put my logo on a link QR?
items.a: Yes. Turn on the logo option and upload a PNG, JPG or GIF image of up to 10 MB. It is placed in the center of the code. Use a simple logo and scan the result to check that it reads well.

items.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes. iPhones and most recent Android phones read QR codes with the camera. On some older Android phones you need a reader app or Google Lens.

whatsapp.other: Opens a chat with you with a message already typed.
whatsapp.lead: Create a QR code that opens a WhatsApp chat with you, with a message already typed if you want. Great for shops, small businesses and customer support. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a WhatsApp QR code

steps.title: Choose your country and type your number
steps.text: In the phone field, select your country and type your number. The country prefix is added for you, and you do not need to type the + sign or spaces.

steps.title: Type a message (optional)
steps.text: If you want, add a message like “Hi, I would like to place an order”. It will appear typed in the chat when someone scans the code. That person decides whether to send it.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with another phone: WhatsApp should open with your number. Then download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

about.title: How a WhatsApp QR works
paragraphs: This code stores a WhatsApp link in the format wa.me/ followed by your number. When scanned, the phone opens WhatsApp with a chat to that number. If you added a message, it appears already typed in the text box.

The other person does not have to save your number in their contacts. They only need to have WhatsApp. Your number must have an active WhatsApp account, and you will receive the message like any other chat.

useCases.title: Where to use a WhatsApp QR
useCases.intro: The advantage of this code is that it removes steps: whoever scans it is already in the chat with you.

items.title: Your shop counter
items.text: Put the code next to the register with a message like “I want to place an order”. Customers write to you without looking for your number.

items.title: Business card
items.text: Add the code to your card so people can contact you with a single scan, without copying the phone number by hand.

items.title: Product packaging
items.text: Stick the code on the box or the bag to handle questions, exchanges or repeat orders through WhatsApp.

items.title: Customer support
items.text: Place it on invoices, manuals or posters in your store with a message that states the reason, for example “I need help with my order”.

items.title: Test it with another phone
items.text: Scan the code with a phone other than yours and check that the chat opens and that the number is the right one.

items.title: Short and clear message
items.text: A brief message, like “Hi, I would like information about…”, encourages people to send it. Avoid long messages.

items.title: Use the number where you answer
items.text: Enter the number you actually reply on. If you change it, you will have to create another code.

items.title: Explain what it is for
items.text: Write a sentence next to the code, like “Message us on WhatsApp”. That way people know what happens when they scan.

items.q: Do I need WhatsApp Business?
items.a: No. It works with a regular WhatsApp account and also with WhatsApp Business. All it needs is for the number to be registered on WhatsApp.

items.q: Can I preload a message?
items.a: Yes. Type the message in the optional field and it will appear already typed in the chat. The person who scans sees it and decides whether to send it: it is not sent automatically.

items.q: Does it work with numbers from any country?
items.a: WhatsApp uses numbers in international format, so the link works for any country. The selector includes Latin American countries, Spain, Portugal and the United States, with Peru as the starting option. If your country is not listed, type the full number with its international prefix (for example, +44 for the United Kingdom) in the phone field. Always test the code before using it.

items.q: What happens if I change my number?
items.a: The code will keep opening a chat with the old number. You will have to create a new code and replace the printed one.

items.q: Does the code expire or have a scan limit?
items.a: No. The number and the message are inside the code. It does not expire, does not count scans and does not depend on our site.

items.q: Can I know how many people scanned it?
items.a: No. You will see the messages you receive in your WhatsApp, as always, but we do not count scans. You cannot know how many people scanned it without them writing to you.

wifi.other: Connects your guests without reading out the password.
wifi.lead: Create a QR code so your guests and customers can join your WiFi without typing the password. Print it, stick it near the router and you are done. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a QR code for your WiFi

steps.title: Type the exact network name
steps.text: Copy your network name (SSID) exactly as it appears on your phone, keeping upper case, lower case and symbols. If it does not match exactly, the phone will not find the network.

steps.title: Enter the password and the security type
steps.text: Type the password and choose WPA/WPA2 (the usual one), WEP or no password. If your network is hidden, tick the “Hidden network” box.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone: it should offer to join the network. Download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF and print it.

about.title: How a WiFi QR works
paragraphs: This code stores your network details as text: the name, the password and the security type. When someone scans it with the camera, the phone shows a prompt to join that network, without typing anything.

The details are inside the pattern and are read on the phone itself, so you do not need internet to read the code. Whoever has the code has your password, so it is best to place it where only the people you want to connect will see it.

useCases.title: Where to use a WiFi QR
useCases.intro: It is useful anywhere that, every day, someone asks you for the password.

items.title: Restaurant or café
items.text: Put the code on the table or at the bar. Customers connect without asking the waiter for the password.

items.title: Airbnb or holiday rental
items.text: Leave it framed in the living room or in the house guide. Your guests will have internet as soon as they arrive.

items.title: Office with visitors
items.text: Print a code for the guest network and place it at reception or in the meeting room.

items.title: Your home
items.text: Stick it on the fridge or near the entrance for friends and family. You will not have to read out a long password every time.

items.title: If you change the password, create the code again
items.text: The code stores the password from that moment. When you change it, the printed code will stop connecting and you will have to generate a new one and replace it.

items.title: Use a guest network
items.text: If your router has a guest network, use that one in the code. That way your visitors do not join the network where your devices are.

items.title: Respect upper case and symbols
items.text: The name and the password are case sensitive. A single different character means it will not connect.

items.title: Print it with good contrast
items.text: Use a dark color, at least 3 x 3 cm. If you frame it, avoid glass with a lot of glare.

items.title: Avoid WEP if you can
items.text: WEP is an old and weak security system. If your router allows it, use WPA2.

items.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes, on most phones. iPhones and recent Android phones read these codes with the camera and offer to join the network. On some older Android phones you may need a reader app or Google Lens.

items.q: What happens if I change the WiFi password?
items.a: The code will keep showing the old password and will no longer connect. Create a new one with the current password and replace the printed one.

items.q: Is it safe to put the password in a QR?
items.a: Anyone who scans the code can use that password. It is only as safe as the place where you put it. Place it only where the people who may connect are, and if you can, use a guest network. The code is created on your device: the password is not sent to any server.

items.q: Do I need internet to scan it?
items.a: Not to read the code: the phone interprets it on its own. Then it connects to your network as if you had typed the password by hand.

items.q: Can I make a QR for a hidden network?
items.a: Yes. Tick the “Hidden network” box before generating the code and type the exact name of the network.

items.q: What if my network has no password?
items.a: Choose “No password” as the security type. The code will only hold the network name. Keep in mind that then anyone will be able to connect.

texto.other: Store a note or some instructions in a code.
texto.lead: Turn a text into a free QR code: some instructions, a note, a product code or a short message. Whoever scans it reads it on their phone. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a text QR code

steps.title: Type or paste your text
steps.text: Type in the text field what you want people to read when they scan. It is stored exactly as you type it.

steps.title: Check the length and customize
steps.text: The more text, the more dots the code has and the harder it is to scan. Keep the text short. If you want, change the color and size or add a logo.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR”, scan it with your phone to check that the full text appears and download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

about.title: What a text QR does
paragraphs: This code stores plain text. When scanned, the phone camera shows that text on the screen, without opening any website or app. Most readers let you copy or share it.

Because the text is inside the code, it can be read without an internet connection. That makes it useful where there is no signal, like a basement, a warehouse or a hike. Like the rest of the codes from this tool, it is static: it cannot be edited afterwards.

useCases.title: Where to use a text QR
useCases.intro: It works when you want to give a short piece of information without building a website.

items.title: Usage instructions
items.text: Stick a code on a device, a tool or a room with the basic steps. Whoever needs them reads them on their phone.

items.title: Notes at events
items.text: Place codes with the schedule, the room rules or a thank-you message on the tables or on the badges.

items.title: Inventory codes
items.text: Label boxes or equipment with a reference, a serial number or the location. Any phone with a QR reader can read it.

items.title: Messages to read offline
items.text: Leave a clue in a treasure hunt or a message on a gift card. It can be read even without signal.

items.title: Short text, easy code
items.text: With few words the code has fewer dots and scans better, even if you print it small.

items.title: Check before downloading
items.text: Once printed, the text cannot be corrected. Reread every word carefully, especially if there are numbers or references.

items.title: For websites and phones, use their type
items.text: If you want a website to open, use the [QR for links](/generador-qr/url). To open a chat, use the [WhatsApp QR](/generador-qr/whatsapp). The phone offers to open them directly, while with a text QR it only sees letters.

items.title: Take care of contrast
items.text: Pick a dark color, since the background is always white, and a minimum size of 2 x 2 cm. Test with your phone before printing.

items.q: How much text can I put in?
items.a: A code has a capacity limit, and the more text, the denser and harder to read it becomes. To make it easy to scan, use one or two sentences. If the text is too long, the code cannot be generated.

items.q: Can it be read without internet?
items.a: Yes. The phone reads the text directly from the code, without connecting to any website. You only need internet to load this page: the code is created on your device.

items.q: Does a text code expire?
items.a: No. The text is inside the code, so it does not expire or have a scan limit.

items.q: Can I change the text after printing it?
items.a: No. It is a static code. If the text changes, create a new code and replace the printed one.

items.q: What is the difference between a text QR and a URL QR?
items.a: The text QR only shows letters on the screen. The URL one opens a web page when scanned. If you want a website to open, use the [QR generator for links](/generador-qr/url).

items.q: Do you store the text I type?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device and the text is not sent to any server. The history of this tool is saved only in your browser.

resenas-google.other: Takes your customers straight to leaving a review.
resenas-google.h1: Free QR code for Google reviews
resenas-google.lead: Create a QR code that takes your customers to the page where they can review your business. Paste the link from your Google profile, download the code and print it. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a QR code for Google reviews

steps.title: Get your business review link
steps.text: Open your Google Business Profile, look for the option to read or ask for reviews and copy the share link. Button names may vary. Below the form you will find a guide with the usual steps.

steps.title: Paste it in the form
steps.text: Paste the full link, which starts with https://. If it does not look like a Google link we will warn you, but you can still use it.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone: the window to write a review of your business should open. Download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF and print it.

about.title: How a Google reviews QR works
paragraphs: This code stores a web link: the one Google gives you to share the reviews of your business. When someone scans it with the camera, the phone opens it and the customer lands on the page where they can write their opinion, without searching for your business on the map.

Google does not publish an official format to build that link from a place identifier, so we do not make one up: you paste the link your profile gives you. The code is created on your device and the link is not sent to any server. It is a static code: if the link changes, you will have to create a new one.

useCases.title: Where to use a reviews QR
useCases.intro: It works best when the customer is happy and has their phone at hand.

items.title: At the counter
items.text: Place it next to the till, on a small stand. Someone who has just paid can leave their opinion while they wait.

items.title: On the table
items.text: Print it on a table sign or on the menu of your bar or restaurant, so the customer writes their review after eating.

items.title: On the receipt or invoice
items.text: Add the code at the bottom of the receipt, the invoice or the delivery note. The opinion arrives when the customer looks over their purchase.

items.title: On a card or flyer
items.text: Include it on your business card, in the order package or on a flyer. It is a discreet reminder for whoever took your product home.

items.title: Do not offer anything in exchange for the review
items.text: Google’s policies do not allow offering incentives in exchange for reviews, neither discounts nor gifts. Ask for the opinion with no conditions.

items.title: Ask at the right moment
items.text: The best moment is right after a good experience: when you hand over the order, finish the service or say goodbye. A friendly line next to the code helps, for example “Did you like it? Tell us”.

items.title: Test the link before printing
items.text: Scan the code with your phone and check that it opens the review window of your business and not that of another place with a similar name.

items.title: Make it easy to scan
items.text: Print it at least 3 x 3 cm, in a dark color on a light background, and place it somewhere with good light. Add a short line that explains what happens when you scan it.

items.title: If your link changes, create a new code
items.text: A static code cannot be edited. If you ever change your link or your profile, the printed code will keep leading to the old one.

faq.title: Questions about the Google reviews QR

items.q: Where do I get my business review link?
items.a: In your Google Business Profile. Look for the option to read or ask for reviews and copy the share link. The names of the options may vary depending on your account and country. Below the form you will find a guide with the usual steps.

items.q: Can I do it with just the name of my business?
items.a: No. Google does not document an official review link format that can be built from a name or a place identifier, so we do not create links on our own. You need to paste the one your profile gives you.

items.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes. The camera of the iPhone and of most Android phones reads the code and opens the link. The person scanning may need to sign in with their Google account to post the review.

items.q: Can I give a discount or a gift to whoever leaves a review?
items.a: It is not advisable. Google’s policies do not allow offering incentives in exchange for reviews. You can ask for the opinion and thank people for it, but without tying it to any reward.

items.q: What happens if I change the link or my profile?
items.a: The code is static: it holds the link as you pasted it and cannot be edited once printed. If the link changes, create a new code and replace the printed one.

items.q: Is my link sent to any server?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device and the link is not sent to any server. The history is saved only in your browser and you can delete it whenever you want.

vcard.other: Share your contact details with a single scan.
vcard.lead: Create a QR code with your name, phone, email and website. Whoever scans it can save you to their contacts without typing anything. Ideal for business cards. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a contact card QR code

steps.title: Fill in your details
steps.text: Enter at least your name or your company name. The rest is optional: last name, job title, phones, email, website, address and a note. Empty fields are not included.

steps.title: Check the content preview
steps.text: Below the form you can see the exact text the code will store. Check that the details are correct.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone: it should offer to save the contact. Download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF and add it to your card.

about.title: How a contact card QR works
paragraphs: A vCard is a standard format for contact cards, the same one phone address books use. The code stores your details as text inside the pattern (vCard 3.0, in UTF-8, so accents and special letters are kept). When scanned, the phone offers to create a new contact with those details.

You do not need internet to read it: the details are inside the code, which is created on your device. The more details you add, the denser the pattern and the larger you will have to print it for it to read well. It is a static code: if you change phone number or job, you will have to create a new one.

useCases.title: Where to use a contact card QR
useCases.intro: It works anywhere someone asks for your details and you would rather not read them out.

items.title: Business card
items.text: Print the code on the back of your card. Whoever gets it saves you on their phone in seconds, without typing your number.

items.title: Trade fair or event
items.text: Put it on your badge or on your stand panel. Contacts save you without having to write your email on paper.

items.title: Résumé
items.text: Add the code to your printed résumé so that whoever receives it can save you on their phone with the camera, without copying your details.

items.title: Shop or local business
items.text: Stick it on the window or on the counter with your phone, your address and your website, so your customers save you to their contacts.

tips.title: Tips for a contact card QR

items.title: Include only what you need
items.text: The more fields, the denser the code. Name, phone, email and website are usually enough, and it reads better, especially if you print it small.

items.title: Write the phone with the country code
items.text: For example +34 600 000 000. That way it also works for whoever saves you from another country.

items.title: Test it with your phone before printing
items.text: The iPhone and most Android cameras offer to save the contact. Some older Android phones may leave out fields, so it is worth checking.

items.title: Leave space for it on the card
items.text: Make it as large as the design allows and leave a white margin around it. A code squeezed into a corner reads worse.

items.title: Create a new one if your details change
items.text: A static code cannot be edited. If you change phone, email or position, generate another and replace the cards.

faq.title: Questions about the contact card QR

items.q: What is a vCard?
items.a: It is a standard format for contact cards. Phones understand it and turn it into a contact you can save in your address book.

items.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes. The iPhone and most Android cameras read the code and offer to save the contact. On some older Android phones fields may be missing when saving, so it is worth testing it with your phone before printing.

items.q: Which details are required?
items.a: Only the name or the company is needed. Everything else is optional and, if you leave it empty, it is not included in the code.

items.q: Can I edit the card after printing it?
items.a: No. It is a static code: the details stay inside the pattern. If they change, create a new code.

items.q: Are my details sent to any server?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device and your contact details are not sent to any server. Anyone who scans the code will see what you wrote, so include only what you want to share.

items.q: Does it support accents and special letters?
items.a: Yes. The content is stored in UTF-8, so names like Núñez or José display correctly. Commas, semicolons and line breaks are written in the correct format so they do not break the card.

ubicacion.other: Opens your address in Google Maps with one scan.
ubicacion.h1: Free Google Maps location QR code
ubicacion.lead: Create a QR code that opens an address or some coordinates in Google Maps. Useful for shops, events and meeting points. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create a location QR code

steps.title: Enter the address or the coordinates
steps.text: Type the address or the name of the place the way you would search for it in Google Maps. If you prefer coordinates, switch to latitude and longitude or press “Use my location”.

steps.title: Check the link
steps.text: Below the form you can see the link the code will store. It is a Google Maps search link.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone: it should open the place on the map. Download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

about.title: How a location QR works
paragraphs: The code stores a Google Maps link with your address or your coordinates. When scanned, the phone opens the Google Maps app if it is installed and, if not, opens the map in the browser. It also works on iPhone.

Write the full address, with street, number and city, so that Maps finds the right place. The “Use my location” button only asks for permission when you press it, and QR Gratis does not send that position to any server. It is a static code: if you move, you will have to create a new one.

useCases.title: Where to use a location QR
useCases.intro: It works when you want someone to reach a place without having to explain the address.

items.title: Shop or premises
items.text: Put it on a flyer, a card or a sign so your customers know how to get to your door.

items.title: Event or wedding
items.text: Include the code in the invitation so guests open the venue on the map with one tap.

items.title: Meeting point
items.text: Mark a pick-up spot, a car park or the entrance to a building site with coordinates, even if it has no clear address.

items.title: Holiday rental
items.text: Add it to the house guide so your guests find the accommodation, the parking or the place to collect the keys.

items.title: Use the full address
items.text: Include street, number, city and, if needed, country. An incomplete address may show another place.

items.title: Check the map before printing
items.text: Scan the code and see that the marker lands where it should. If not, try coordinates, which are more exact.

items.title: Use coordinates when there is no address
items.text: In a park, on a beach or in a field, use latitude and longitude. You can press “Use my location” while you are there.

items.title: If you move, create a new code
items.text: The code is static. If you change address, the printed code will keep leading to the old one.

items.title: Add a line next to the code
items.text: Write something like “How to get here” near the code, so whoever sees it knows what happens when they scan it.

items.q: Does it open in Google Maps or in the browser?
items.a: If the phone has the Google Maps app, it opens there. If not, the map opens in the browser. It also works on iPhone.

items.q: What is the difference between an address and coordinates?
items.a: An address is easier to type, but Maps may interpret it differently. Coordinates (latitude and longitude) point to an exact spot and are useful for places without a clear address.

items.q: What does the “Use my location” button do?
items.a: It asks your browser for permission to know your current position and fills in the latitude and longitude. It only does so when you press it. If you refuse, you can type the address or the coordinates by hand. QR Gratis does not send your position to any server.

items.q: Which coordinate format does it accept?
items.a: Decimal degrees, for example 40.4168 and -3.7038. Latitude goes from -90 to 90 and longitude from -180 to 180. If you type a decimal comma (40,4168), we convert it to a point.

items.q: Can I change the place after printing the code?
items.a: No. It is a static code: the place stays inside the pattern. If you move or change the meeting point, create a new code.

items.q: Is my address sent to any server?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device. It only contains a Google Maps link with the address or coordinates you typed, and anyone who scans the code will be able to see it.

email.other: Opens a ready-written email with your address.
email.lead: Create a QR code that opens a new email with your address, a subject and a message already typed. Ideal for asking for quotes or collecting enquiries. No sign-up and no expiry.

how.title: How to create an email QR code

steps.title: Enter the recipient email
steps.text: Enter the address that will receive the messages. We will check that it has a valid format.

steps.title: Add a subject and a message (optional)
steps.text: You can leave a subject and a text already typed, for example “I would like a quote”. Whoever scans only has to review it and press send.

steps.title: Generate, test and download
steps.text: Press “Generate QR” and scan it with your phone: it should open your email app with the message ready. Download the file as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

about.title: How an email QR works
paragraphs: The code stores a mailto link with the address, the subject and the message. When scanned, the phone opens the email app with a new message already prepared. Nothing is sent on its own: the person reviews it and presses send.

Spaces, accents and symbols such as & are encoded so they do not break the link. The code is created on your device and does not depend on any service. It is a static code: if you change your email address, you will have to create a new one.

useCases.title: Where to use an email QR
useCases.intro: It is useful when you want people to write to you without typing your address.

items.title: Asking for a quote
items.text: Put it on your van, on a flyer or on your card with the subject “Quote” already typed, to receive tidy messages.

items.title: Customer service
items.text: Add it to the packaging or the receipt so the customer writes to you with their problem, with the subject already prepared.

items.title: Suggestions and feedback
items.text: Place it in the shop with the subject “Suggestion”. It is a simple way to collect opinions in private.

items.title: Job offer
items.text: Stick up a “We are hiring” sign with a prepared email so people send their résumé.

items.title: Use a clear subject
items.text: A subject like “Kitchen remodel quote” helps you sort the messages you receive.

items.title: Keep the message short
items.text: A couple of lines is enough. The more text, the denser the code and the harder it is to read.

items.title: Use an address you will keep
items.text: If you change email, the printed code will keep pointing to the old one. A business email usually lasts longer than a personal one.

items.title: Test it with your email app
items.text: Scan it with your phone and see how the message looks before printing. Each phone opens its default email app.

items.title: Remember the address is visible
items.text: Whoever scans the code will see your address. Avoid putting a private email in a public place.

items.q: Is the email sent automatically when scanned?
items.a: No. A new message opens with the address, the subject and the text prepared. The person reviews it and decides whether to send it.

items.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes. The camera opens the email app you have set as default. If none is set up, the phone may ask you to choose one.

items.q: Can I leave the subject and the message empty?
items.a: Yes. Only the address is required. Empty fields are not included in the code.

items.q: What happens with accents, spaces and the & symbol?
items.a: They are encoded so the link does not break. You can write accents or something like “Café & more” and the message will arrive as you wrote it.

items.q: Can I change the address after printing?
items.a: No, it is a static code. If the address or the subject changes, create a new code.

items.q: Are my address and message sent to any server?
items.a: No. The code is created on your device and does not go through any server of ours. Anyone who scans the code will see the address and the text you wrote.
